title: Risk‑based credibility assessment of two implicit FEA models for a coronary stent under fatigue and radial strength mechanisms per ASME V&V 40
runhead: Credibility of stent FEA for fatigue and radial strength
device: Balloon-expandable coronary stent intended for scaffolding diseased coronary arteries

models.name: Model 1 — Stent Lattice Implicit FEA
models.what_it_computes: Element-level stresses and strains in the bare stent under crimping, balloon expansion, and cyclic lumen pressure and curvature; predicts local fatigue damage indices and load–displacement behavior using an implicit static/steady cyclic solution.

models.name: Model 2 — Stent-in-Artery Implicit FEA
models.what_it_computes: Coupled response of the expanded stent with a deformable arterial wall during radial compression and cyclic bending; computes radial crush resistance, contact states, and strain ranges at hotspots using an implicit quasi-static formulation.

mechanisms.name: Pulsatile fatigue (pressure-driven strain cycling)
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Cyclic intraluminal pressure and vessel curvature drive strain ranges in stent struts that govern fatigue life, influencing risk of late fracture.

mechanisms.name: Bending-induced fatigue (cardiac motion)
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Axial and out-of-plane bending of the stented segment during the cardiac cycle amplifies local curvature and notch effects, creating fatigue hot spots.

mechanisms.name: Radial crush strength (diametral compression)
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Resistance to external radial loading preserves lumen patency and scaffolding, supporting bench equivalence to compression tests for labeling.

clear_factors: Relevance of the validation activities to the COU

deviation.detail: All credibility activities are scored per factor for each model × mechanism on a 0–5 Fitness-for-Decision scale (0=no usable evidence; 5=decision-grade evidence), and the paper reports these numeric scores in a results matrix.

sections: Device and computational models (implicit FEA formulations and outputs)

Context of use: virtual bench testing to supplement ISO-like fatigue endurance and radial compression evidence for labeling; Model risk level: medium, because decisions inform bench equivalence and labeling but do not directly control clinical deployment. Rationale: an incorrect prediction could mischaracterize endurance or scaffolding claims, mitigated by mandatory bench testing that remains primary.
Mechanisms of interest and their experimental comparators

Credibility plan constrained to seven factors: Discretization error; Model inputs; Numerical code verification; Numerical solver error; Output comparison; Relevance of the validation activities to the COU; Software quality assurance
Numerical code verification (analytic patch tests and manufactured solutions; both models)
Numerical solver error (residual tolerances, contact convergence, path-following robustness; per model × mechanism)
Discretization error (systematic mesh refinement, strut-thickness sensitivity, contact discretization; per model × mechanism)
Model inputs (geometry, material law, boundary conditions, loading amplitudes; traceability and uncertainty bounds; per model × mechanism)
Output comparison (bench-referenced radial stiffness and crush strength; fatigue strain-range and life proxies vs coupons and stent samples; per model × mechanism)
Relevance of the validation activities to the COU (mapping test articles, loading spectra, and measurement outputs to decision needs; per model × mechanism)
Software quality assurance (toolchain description, change control, and run-time logs noted briefly)
Credibility results matrix (0–5 Fitness-for-Decision scores reported for each factor across both models and all three mechanisms, with short justifications per cell)
Discussion (implications for labeling support and model use boundaries within the stated COU)
Limitations (scope restricted to seven credibility factors; no claims beyond fatigue and radial strength)
Conclusions and next steps (focused improvements for low-scoring factor–mechanism pairs)
